title: Noahic Lineages of China, Persia, India, Kashmir, Sri Lanka, Burma & Tibet

nodes.name: 'Abur (Amur) b. Japheth → Yarej → Na'ur → Lotsatis (1st King of China at Anku)
nodes.era: Post-Flood Eastern Dispersion (Al-Mas'udi Vol. I pp. 312-313)
nodes.role: Classical Arabic Japhethic Ancestry of the Early Sovereigns of China
sources: Al-Mas'udi Meadows of Gold Vol. I pp. 312-313
nodes.notes: Al-Mas'udi explicitly derives the Chinese sovereigns from Japheth b. Noah: 'The majority of the children of Abur followed the course of the river to the extremity of China... Their first king in this new settlement was Lotsatis ben Na'ur ben Yarej ben Abur ben Yafeth ben Nuh' at Anku.

nodes.name: 'Arun → 'Abirun → 'Athinan → Jaraban (Early Noahic Chinese Monarchs of Mas'udi)
nodes.role: Early Chinese Dynasty in Al-Mas'udi's Universal Chronicle
sources: Al-Mas'udi Meadows of Gold Vol. I pp. 313-317
nodes.notes: Al-Mas'udi continues Lotsatis's lineage through 'Arun, 'Abirun, 'Athinan (bordering the Turks, descendants of his uncle), Jaraban (who sent ships to India & Babylon) & his temple-building lawgiver successor.

nodes.name: Hind & Sind (Progenitors of India & Sindh in Tabari & Mas'udi)
nodes.era: Post-Flood South Asia (Al-Tabari Vol. 2 pp. 15-17; Al-Mas'udi)
nodes.role: Noahic Anchors of India & Sindh via Ham (Cush) and Shem (Joktan)
nodes.notes: Al-Tabari records both major traditions linking India to Noah: (1) Indians & Sindis descending from Ham -> Cush/Canaan (p. 15), and (2) Ibn 'Abbas & Hisham al-Kalbi's line Shem -> Arphaxad -> Shelah -> Eber -> Qahtan (Joktan) -> Buqayin, father of Hind & Sind (p. 17).

nodes.name: King Mahāsammata (= Manu) → Okkaka (= Ikshvaku) → Śākya Royal Stem
nodes.era: Pali & Buddhist Royal Stem (Mahavamsa Ch. II p. 80)
nodes.role: Solar-Buddhist Dynastic Bridge Linking India, Sri Lanka, Burma & Tibet
nodes.notes: The Pali Mahavamsa opens its royal pedigree with first elected king Mahāsammata (cognate of Manu) -> Roja -> Mandhatar -> Okkaka (Pali form of Solar Dynasty founder Ikshvaku!) -> the Śākya clan of Kapilavastu.

nodes.name: Kashmir Kings (Kalhana's Rajatarangini): Gonanda I (Kurukshetra) → Ashoka of Kashmir
nodes.era: Kurukshetra to 3rd c. BCE (Kalhana's Rajatarangini Book I)
nodes.role: Historical Kashmiri Dynasty Synchronized with Pandavas & Emperor Ashoka
nodes.notes: Kalhana's Rajatarangini begins Kashmir's royal chronology at the Kurukshetra War under Gonanda I (contemporary of the Pandavas) and directly includes Emperor Ashoka (who exchanged envoys with Ptolemy II of Egypt!).

nodes.name: Sri Lanka (Mahavamsa): Prince Vijaya (1st King of Lanka, 543 BCE) & Thera Mahinda (Son of Ashoka)
nodes.role: Founding Sinhalese Dynasty & Mauryan Buddhist Mission to Lanka
nodes.notes: The Mahavamsa connects Sri Lanka's first monarch Vijaya (landing on the exact day of Buddha's Parinirvana) -> Devanampiya Tissa with Emperor Ashoka's own son Mahinda and daughter Sanghamitta.

nodes.name: Burma (Glass Palace Chronicle): King Abhiraza (Śākya Prince of Kapilavastu → Founder of Tagaung)
nodes.role: Burmese Royal Origin Descended from Mahāsammata & Okkaka / Śākya
sources: Glass Palace Chronicle of the Kings of Burma (Pe Maung Tin & Luce)
nodes.notes: The Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle) traces the founding kings of Burma to Śākya prince Abhiraza, descendant of Mahāsammata and Okkaka (Ikshvaku), who marched from northern India to build Tagaung.

nodes.name: Tibet (The Blue Annals): Nyatri Tsenpo (1st Yarlung King, Śākya/Licchavi Stem) → Songtsen Gampo
nodes.era: Ancient Yarlung to 7th c. CE (Roerich The Blue Annals Book I)
nodes.role: Tibetan Royal Lineage Derived from India's Śākya / Licchavi House
sources: The Blue Annals (Deb-ther sngon-po, George Roerich tr., Book I)
nodes.notes: 'Gos Lo-tsā-ba's Blue Annals Book I opens the Royal Chronicle of Tibet with the Indian Śākya/Licchavi origin of Tibet's first king Nyatri Tsenpo (gNya'-khri btsan-po) descending to Buddhist unifier Songtsen Gampo.

edges.label: Al-Mas'udi Meadows of Gold Vol. I pp. 312-313: Majority of children of 'Abur b. Yafeth b. Nuh settled China; first king Lotsatis b. Na'ur b. Yarej b. 'Abur b. Japheth b. Noah
Cross-cultural chronicler synchronization of China's Noahic founding era
Al-Mas'udi Vol. I pp. 313-317: Successors of Lotsatis who initiated Chinese maritime trade to India & Babylon, temples & law codes
Cave of Treasures p. 143: Noah sent 4th son Yonton (Jonitus) to the Far East ('Land of the Rising Sun')
John Jackson 1752 Chronological Antiquities & James Anderson 1732: 18th-c. universal chronography identifying Chinese sovereign Fo-hi (Fuxi) with Noah
Al-Tabari Vol. 1 p. 369 & Mirkhwand p. 50 (Imam Ghazali): Persian/Islamic chroniclers equating Gayomart (Kayumars) with Adam
Mirkhwand p. 50 & Al-Mas'udi p. 77: Persian historians identifying Gayomart with Umaym b. Lud b. Aram b. Shem b. Noah
Al-Tabari Vol. 2 p. 15 & Mirkhwand p. 50: Genealogy tracing Persian kings back to Jayumart / Gomer b. Japheth b. Noah
Al-Tabari Vol. 2 p. 15: Cyrus the Mede, conqueror of Belshazzar, descended from Madai b. Japheth
Al-Tabari Vol. 2 p. 15 & Al-Mas'udi: Indians (Hind) & Sindis descend from Ham b. Noah via Cush/Canaan
Al-Tabari Vol. 2 p. 17 (Ibn 'Abbas / Hisham al-Kalbi): Alternate tradition tracing Hind & Sind to Buqayin b. Qahtan (Joktan) b. Eber b. Shem
Chronicler bridge linking Noahic Hind/Sind to India's Great Flood survivor Vaivasvata Manu
Great Flood survivor Vaivasvata Manu (Shatapatha Brahmana / Matsya Purana) — classic Noahic cognate
Mahavamsa Ch. II p. 80 & Glass Palace Chronicle: Buddhist royal stem from first king Mahāsammata -> Okkaka (Ikshvaku) -> Śākya clan
Okkaka / Ikshvaku -> Śākya clan -> King Shuddhodana -> Siddhartha Gautama Buddha
Kalhana's Rajatarangini Book I (Stein): Kashmir chronology anchored to Pandavas/Kurukshetra & Emperor Ashoka (who links historically to Ptolemy II!)
Mahavamsa Ch. II-VII: Vijaya arrives on the day of Buddha's Parinirvana; Mahinda son of Ashoka brings Buddhism to Lanka
Son Mahinda & daughter Sanghamitta of Emperor Ashoka
Glass Palace Chronicle of the Kings of Burma: Traces Burmese kings directly to Śākya prince Abhiraza, descendant of Mahāsammata & Okkaka/Ikshvaku
Roerich The Blue Annals Book I (Royal Chronicle of Tibet): Traces 1st Tibetan king Nyatri Tsenpo to the Indian Śākya/Licchavi lineage of Mahāsammata & Ikshvaku
